items.name: ZeroDrift Anchor 3.0
items.summary: ZeroDrift's Anchor 3.0 is the first family of small language models built to enforce regulatory and company rules on AI-generated communications before they're sent. It caught 95.5% of FINRA violations in the company's new benchmark — beating the strongest frontier model tested, GPT-5.6 Sol — while running up to 34x faster and 12x cheaper.

items.name: Bell + Cohere cybersecurity AI
items.summary: Bell Canada and Cohere launched a cybersecurity-focused LLM trained on Bell Cyber's operational knowledge to speed up threat investigations inside Bell's Autonomous Security Operations Centre. The domain-specific model summarizes complex security data and standardizes investigative workflows while keeping analysts in control of consequential decisions.

items.name: Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 is its most powerful model to date, taking the top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (58) and rivaling the top-tier Fable 5.1 at 40% lower cost. It adds 'preserved thinking' — a defense against model distillation — and is 85% less likely than Opus 5 to attempt bypassing its safety boundaries.

items.name: GPT-6 Sol & Luna
items.summary: OpenAI added two cheaper tiers to the GPT-6 family: Sol for complex workloads like coding, and Luna for high-volume tasks like extraction and summarization, with API prices cut 50% versus GPT-5.6. OpenAI claims GPT-6 Sol at xhigh effort outperforms Claude Opus 5 at max effort on AutomationBench at just 9% of the cost per task.

items.name: StepFun Step 5 Preview
items.summary: StepFun's Step 5 Preview is a ~600B-parameter proprietary reasoning model positioned as China's cheapest frontier AI model yet. At $1.00/$2.70 per million input/output tokens it undercuts every comparable reasoning model while delivering frontier-level benchmark performance at ~100 tokens/sec.
